Bhuvneshwar Kumar Insists Bowlers Can Still Control T20 Cricket After India's Win in Wellington

Veteran Pacer Returns to T20I Setup

Indian fast bowler Bhuvneshwar Kumar has expressed confidence that bowlers can still dictate terms in the modern, batter-heavy era of T20 cricket. Speaking to reporters following India's victory in the third T20I against New Zealand in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the 36-year-old pacer emphasized that adaptability and precise execution remain the primary tools for success.

Bhuvneshwar has returned to the Indian T20I squad after a gap of nearly four years, earning his recall following consistent performances in the Indian Premier League (IPL).

Key Takeaways from the Press Conference

  • Bowlers Retain Control: Bhuvneshwar acknowledged that conditions and small boundaries often favor batters and the margin of error is extremely low, but maintained that bowlers ultimately decide where the ball pitches.
  • Adaptability is Crucial: The veteran emphasized that consistent and adaptable bowlers continue to thrive by adjusting quickly to match situations.
  • Evolution of the Game: Comparing the format to his debut in 2012, he noted that contemporary batters look to attack every single delivery rather than consolidating after early runs.
  • Future Outlook: Bhuvneshwar stated he is not looking too far ahead regarding his international future or ODI ambitions, intending to stay grounded and play domestic tournaments like the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy.

  • Reported Result: India secured a win in the match, as reported by wire services.
